findings.title: Readiness can be falsely satisfied by a foreign listener on the port
findings.problem: The HTTP /health probe only checks that something answers on the port. If the port is already bound (e.g. the pre-existing 8080 instance with the default port), the new proxy exits on bind failure, but the probe hits the other instance, so status can show Running/Ready while the managed process is crash-looping. proxy:up then reports success.
findings.fix: Fail fast if the port is already listening before starting (e.g. a preflight check in proxy:up), or verify the managed PID owns the listener.

findings.title: Failed proxy:up leaves the detached supervisor running and a crash-loop
findings.problem: With `set -eu`, if proxy-wait-ready.sh times out (up to 120s), the task exits non-zero but process-compose stays detached. restart: on_failure with a 2s backoff retries forever. A second `proxy:up` then conflicts with the existing socket or supervisor.
findings.fix: On wait failure, run `process-compose down -U` (trap or `||`) before exiting non-zero, and cap restarts with max_restarts.

findings.title: Failed readiness leaves detached supervisor running
findings.problem: proxy:up starts process-compose with -D, then proxy-wait-ready.sh exits 1 after 120s. Nothing stops the supervisor. With restart: on_failure the failing proxy keeps restarting. The next proxy:up then fails or conflicts with the leftover supervisor and its socket. A crash-looping binary keeps retrying with no restart limit.
findings.fix: On wait failure, run `process-compose down -U` (for example via a trap or `|| { process-compose down -U; exit 1; }`) before returning non-zero. Also set max_restarts in availability.

findings.title: Preflight only checks 127.0.0.1 while the host is configurable
findings.problem: The proxy binds COPILOT_PROXY_RS_HOST, which may be non-loopback. The preflight and the readiness probe both hit only 127.0.0.1. A listener on another interface is missed. The probe can then pass against the wrong listener, or fail if the host is not loopback.
findings.fix: Preflight the same host the proxy binds, or reject a non-loopback host in the managed config.

findings.title: Restart readiness wait can race a stale Ready state
findings.problem: proxy:restart calls wait-ready, which accepts any Running/Ready row. If the restart returns before the status resets, the check can pass on the old state. Restart also has no handling for a supervisor that is not running.
findings.fix: Wait for the PID to change or for the process to leave Ready first. Fail clearly if the socket is missing.

findings.title: Readiness check parses process-compose table by fixed column positions
findings.problem: awk matches $2/$4/$6 of `process list --output wide`. Column layout is not a stable interface. The pin is 1.124.0, but a bump or a status text containing spaces silently makes proxy:up and proxy:restart time out after 120s even when the proxy is healthy.
findings.fix: Use `process-compose process list -U -o json` (jq or python) and check status==Running and is_ready==Ready, or poll `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health` after preflight.

findings.title: Unix socket path under .process-compose can exceed the sun_path limit
findings.problem: PC_SOCKET_PATH is {{config_root}}/.process-compose/pc.sock. macOS allows about 104 bytes and Linux about 108. A deeply nested checkout makes `process-compose up` fail with an opaque bind error. README and preflight do not mention or check this.
findings.fix: Have proxy:up check the path length and fail with a clear message, or fall back to a short path such as $TMPDIR/pc-<hash>.sock. Document the limit.

findings.title: Proxy and supervisor logs grow without bound
findings.problem: log_location and PC_LOG_FILE write to .process-compose/ with no rotation. README mentions the location but gives no retention guidance for long-running operators.
findings.fix: Add a logging.rotation block (max_size, max_backups, max_age) or document manual cleanup.

findings.title: bootstrap.sh does not verify prerequisites or tell the user how to activate mise
findings.problem: A fresh-machine run installs mise via curl|sh into ~/.local/bin but does not persist PATH or activation. A later `mise run proxy:up` fails with 'command not found' in a new shell. It also does not check that cargo exists, which proxy:up needs. The README only says 'With Rust installed'.
findings.fix: After install, print a hint to add ~/.local/bin to PATH or activate mise. Warn if `cargo` is missing.

findings.title: Readiness probe/preflight hardcode 127.0.0.1 while proxy host is configurable
findings.problem: With COPILOT_PROXY_RS_HOST=::1 or a specific non-127.0.0.1 loopback address, the proxy binds there but the probe, preflight and wait-ready all use 127.0.0.1. `proxy:up` then times out after 120s and tears the supervisor down. The README acknowledges this constraint but nothing enforces it. Preflight also misses conflicts on the configured host.
findings.fix: Use ${COPILOT_PROXY_RS_HOST:-127.0.0.1} for probe host and preflight (mapping 0.0.0.0 to 127.0.0.1), or document loopback-only. Alternatively reject incompatible hosts in preflight with a clear error.

findings.title: proxy:up with a lingering supervisor is not guarded
findings.problem: If the supervisor is alive but the proxy is stopped or crashed (max_restarts exhausted), the port is free so preflight passes and a second 'process-compose up -D' is launched against the same socket. The failure path then runs 'down -U', which may kill the original supervisor. A stale socket after a crash or kill -9 also makes proxy:restart (which only tests -S) fail with a raw connection error, a…
findings.fix: Fail early in proxy:up if the control socket already answers (e.g. 'process-compose process list -U' succeeds), telling the user to run proxy:down or proxy:restart. Also detect and clear stale sockets in preflight and document recovery (e.g. removing .process-compose/).

findings.title: proxy:up waits the full 120s if the supervisor fails to start
findings.problem: The wait loop never checks whether the detached supervisor or the socket exists. A failed 'up -D' or a crashed proxy is only reported after the 120s timeout.
findings.fix: Fail fast when the socket is missing after a short grace period, or when the process status is Error/Completed.

findings.title: Unix socket path can exceed OS sun_path limit in deep checkouts
findings.problem: PC_SOCKET_PATH is {{config_root}}/.process-compose/pc.sock. macOS limits Unix socket paths to about 104 bytes and Linux to about 108. Long worktree or home paths make `proxy:up` fail with an opaque bind error. Neither the task nor the README warns about this or validates it.
findings.fix: Add a length check in proxy-preflight.sh with a clear error. Alternatively allow overriding PC_SOCKET_PATH, for example to a short path under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or /tmp. Make the `[ -S .process-compose/pc.sock ]` check in proxy:restart follow the override.

findings.title: Bootstrap pipes an unpinned remote installer to sh and does not verify the prerequisites it needs
findings.problem: `curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh` installs an unpinned, unverified mise on a fresh machine. The script only warns when cargo is missing, so it reports success while `proxy:up` will fail. It also never checks for curl.
findings.fix: Pin the mise version (MISE_VERSION=... in the install command) or document the risk. Check for curl before use. Consider failing, or printing an explicit next step, when cargo is missing.

findings.title: proxy:logs and proxy:status give no guidance when the supervisor is down, and logs are unbounded
findings.problem: `proxy:logs` and `proxy:status` run process-compose directly. With no supervisor they print a raw socket-connect error, unlike `proxy:restart`, which has a friendly message. .process-compose/*.log files have no rotation or size limit, and the README does not mention it.
findings.fix: Add a shared guard for the missing socket with a hint to run proxy:up. Set log rotation in process-compose.yaml (log_configuration.rotation) or document cleanup.

findings.fix: Add mkdir -p "{{config_root}}/.process-compose" to proxy:up in addition to the socket directory.

findings.title: proxy:down is not idempotent and fails with no helpful message
findings.problem: proxy:status, proxy:logs and proxy:restart call proxy-require-supervisor.sh for a clear 'use proxy:up' message. proxy:down runs raw `process-compose down -U`, so it exits nonzero with a raw connection error when nothing is running or the socket is stale. A crash also leaves the stale socket in place until the next proxy:up.
findings.fix: Route proxy:down through the same check. If no supervisor answers, remove the stale socket, print 'not running' and exit 0.

findings.title: Supervisor dies if the proxy stays down after max_restarts, with no operator note
findings.problem: restart: on_failure with max_restarts: 5 and 2s backoff leaves the process Error or Completed after about 10s of crash-looping. For a port conflict that appears after startup, the supervisor stays alive with a dead proxy. README does not mention this. proxy:status then shows a failure but proxy:up refuses to start because a supervisor exists.
findings.fix: Document the recovery path (proxy:down, then proxy:up). Optionally have preflight detect a running supervisor whose proxy is not Running.

findings.title: Bootstrap pipes a remote install script to sh with no integrity check
findings.problem: `curl -fsSL https://mise.run | ... sh` runs remote code on a fresh machine. The version is pinned through MISE_VERSION, but the script itself is unverified and the pinned v2026.10.24 is only exercised if the network is reachable. README does not state the trust implication.
findings.fix: Document that the installer is fetched from mise.run, or offer a brew/package-manager path or checksum verification.
